newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts drop sharply on profit-taking,politics.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts drop sharply on profit-taking,politics.

text.p: UK gilts dropped sharply in late trade on profit-taking and year-end jitters about domestic politics, analysts said.
The March long gilt contract ended 22/32 lower at 108-19/32.

"I think it's the beginning of political jitters ahead of the New Year -- the realisation that the gilt market is not going to be supported by politics," said Nigel Richardson at Yamaichi International.
Analysts also said retail price data, while in line with market expectations, confirmed that the short-term outlook for prices was not positive.
Underlying inflation was unchanged at 3.3 percent in November. "It does seem clear that the Chancellor is going to miss his 2.5 percent target," said Katy Peters, an analyst at Daiwa Europe.
She said gilts had done reasonably well after U.S. inflation data and when it became clear that there had been no change in official UK interest rates at Wednesday's monetary meeting.
CBI output data had also lent some support before profit-taking emerged in late trade, she said. The softer tone in Treasuries and Bunds also weighed on gilts.
The gilt/Bund spread at 10 years widened to 189 basis points from the previous 187, having gone above 190 during the session.
March short sterling was up one basis point at 93.43, implying official interest rates of around 6.60 percent at the end of the first quarter compared with the present 6.0 percent.
